headline: FIRST MAJESTIC SILVER Q3: SAN DIMAS LABOUR DISPUTE CUTS 12 DAYS OF PRODUCTION — 3.4M OZ SILVER, 29,552 OZ GOLD REPORTED
snippet: First Majestic Silver reported Q3 2026 production of 3.4 million silver ounces and 29,552 gold ounces (5.2 million AgEq oz) as a 12-day labour dispute at its flagship San Dimas mine shaved output below the prior-year record of 3.9 million silver ounces. Year-to-date production of roughly 10.75 million AgEq oz keeps the company on track for its revised 2026 guidance of 14.6–15.5 million attributable ounces, with Q3 conference call details and a share repurchase program renewal also announced.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACTS SMASH 19-YEAR NOMINAL RECORD AT $96.50/LB — BUT PRODUCERS ARE SELLING OFF ANYWAY
snippet: The long-term uranium contract price hit $96.50 per pound in August 2026 and held there through September, surpassing the prior nominal peak of $95/lb set in mid-2007 — a milestone analysts note is less dramatic in inflation-adjusted terms than the headline implies. Spot uranium sits at $89.63/lb and nuclear producers have paradoxically weakened on profit-taking and rising yields, even as TD Cowen projects a 42-million-pound supply deficit by 2035 and utility contracting remains at a record pace.

headline: COPPER PLUNGES 1.2% TO $14,300/T AS OIL SURGE REVIVES RATE HIKE FEARS — DEMAND OUTLOOK TRUMPS CHILE SUPPLY RISK
snippet: LME three-month copper fell 1.2% to US$14,300.50 per metric ton on October 8 as surging oil prices revived inflation concerns and potential rate-hike risk outweighed ongoing strike threats at Chilean and Philippine copper mines. Traders noted that demand-side macro fears — specifically the possibility that higher oil prices feed into inflation and delay central bank easing — are currently weighing more heavily on copper than the supply disruptions that had supported prices earlier in the week.

headline: CODELCO PROBE WIDENS: CHILE PROSECUTOR TARGETS A SECOND MINE DIVISION IN COPPER PRODUCTION OVERSTATEMENT SCANDAL
snippet: The O'Higgins regional prosecutor announced on October 6 he is examining possible second artificial inflation of copper production at Codelco's Ministro Hales and El Salvador divisions, widening a criminal investigation that already covers roughly 27,000 tonnes of copper mistakenly booked as finished product at Chuquicamata in December 2025. One senior executive has been dismissed and seven others disciplined; Chile's congress is running a parallel special investigative commission into the world's largest copper miner as an external forensic audit remains underway.

headline: CRITICAL METALS TANBREEZ GETS GREENLAND MINING GREEN LIGHT THROUGH 2050 — WORLD'S LARGEST UNDEVELOPED RE DEPOSIT CLEARS KEY GATE
source_name: Mining Weekly / Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML)
snippet: Greenland's government signed off on Critical Metals' mining and closure plans at the Tanbreez project on September 29, valid through September 2050, covering the full suite of target minerals including dysprosium, terbium, neodymium, praseodymium, zirconium and hafnium. The approvals unlock initial throughput of 85,000 t/y (scalable to 425,000 t/y) but construction still requires activity-specific operating permits under Sections 120–121 of Greenland's Mineral Activities Act; shares rose ~4% before settling.

headline: USA RARE EARTH, MP MATERIALS FALL FOR A SECOND STRAIGHT DAY — ANTIMONY SLIDES 4% AS US-CHINA THAW GRINDS DOWN CRITICAL MINERALS TRADE PREMIUM
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) fell an additional 4%, MP Materials (MP) dropped 5%, and United States Antimony (UAMY) shed 4% on October 8 — a second consecutive session of broad critical-minerals selling with no company-specific catalyst. The sustained selling confirms that the thematic premium baked into domestically produced rare earth and strategic metals stocks is deflating as diplomatic warming between Washington and Beijing reduces the perceived urgency of supply-chain decoupling.

headline: URANIUM WEEK: U308 BUCKS RISING YIELDS AS LONG-TERM CONTRACTS HIT RECORD AND UTILITY CONTRACTING PACE HOLDS
snippet: FNArena's weekly uranium market wrap notes that uranium spot and term prices held firm through the week ending October 6 despite bond yield headwinds that pressured most growth assets, with the term price's new all-time record at $96.50/lb reinforcing analyst expectations that utility demand is going to outpace supply. Kazatomprom maintained 2026 output guidance at 27,500–29,000 tonnes despite record term prices, underscoring a market where incremental supply capacity is not expanding to match the contracting wave.

headline: GOLD MINING STOCKS ENTER Q4 ON SHAKY FOOTING — SEEKING ALPHA: "NOT CLEAR THE COAST IS CLEAR" AS OIL-DRIVEN RATE FEARS RESURFACE
snippet: A Seeking Alpha sector review published October 8 says gold mining stocks had a better Q3 than Q2 but lost significant ground near the quarter's end as oil prices drove alternating macro narratives on rate policy — leaving miners starting Q4 with unresolved momentum. The author argues that the coast is unlikely to be clear for gold equities until the inflation-versus-easing debate settles, making selective position sizing more important than broad-sector exposure at current levels.

headline: BULLION GOLD DRILLS 1.73 G/T AU OVER 13.4 METRES AT TERRAGOLD, QUEBEC — CORE INTERVAL HITS 3.80 G/T AU OVER 4.4M
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Bullion Gold (TSXV: BGD)
snippet: Bullion Gold (TSXV: BGD) released assay results from diamond drill hole TG-04 at its Terragold property in Quebec, returning 1.73 g/t gold over 13.4 metres including a higher-grade core of 3.80 g/t gold over 4.4 metres. The result advances definition drilling at a deposit that carries the structural geology common to the Val-d'Or gold camp, adding to a growing body of drill data ahead of a resource estimate.

headline: GOGOLD RESOURCES DROPS 6% ON SECTOR WEAKNESS — SILVER-GOLD MEXICO JUNIOR HITS CORRECTION TERRITORY WITHOUT COMPANY NEWS
snippet: GoGold Resources (TSX: GGD), the Canadian operator focused on silver-gold projects in Jalisco and Durango, Mexico, fell 5.97% on October 7 with no company-specific news driving the move — a decline analysts attribute to broad mining-sector sentiment deterioration rather than any change in the company's operational or financial fundamentals. The move pushes GoGold into technical correction territory and mirrors the pattern of sector re-rating risk that has pressured mid-tier precious metals names since gold's pullback from its September highs.
